result.stdout:
Aetheris — exact code-first CAD

Usage: aetheris <command> [options]

Commands:
  validate   Check Firmament source without materializing geometry.
  build      Compile Firmament to exact STEP AP242.
  mesh       Export a supported exact B-rep as STL or topology-preserving OBJ.
  view       Build/open a model in Cadmata.
  inspect    Inspect Firmament semantics or STEP topology.
  analyze    Analyze STEP topology and analytic surfaces.
  fea        Compile and solve a Firmament linear-elastic analysis and export Abaqus verification input.
  drawing    Compile a Firmament Drawing Template to DrawingIR, SVG, vector A4 PDF, and native editable PPTX.
  asm        Inspect, execute, import, and export Firmament V2 assemblies.
  modules    Inspect built-in engineering Modules and capabilities.
  sheetmetal Inspect/recover sheet semantics and generate manufacturing flat-pattern SVG.
  verify     Build/reimport and verify a model.
  reconstruct  Experimentally reconstruct a structured mesh from triangle PLY input.

Global options:
  -h, --help       Show help.
  -v, --version    Show CLI version.

Examples:
  aetheris validate bracket.firmament
  aetheris build bracket.firmament
  aetheris view bracket.firmament
  aetheris analyze imported.step --json
  aetheris fea plate-with-hole.firmament --out-dir artifacts --json
  aetheris drawing compile bearing-block-drawing.firmament --out-dir artifacts/drawing --json
  aetheris asm inspect bearing-module.firmament --json
  aetheris sheetmetal flatten bracket.firmament --step bracket-flat.step --svg bracket-flat.svg --json
  aetheris reconstruct mesh scan.ply --mode fast --out scan-remesh.obj --report scan-report.json

Run 'aetheris <command> --help' for command-specific usage.

result.stdout:
Build canonical Firmament V2 .firmament input into STEP output.
Explicitly versioned Firmament V1 TOON/JSON files remain readable through the historical compatibility route and emit one warning.
Legacy JSON .firmasm is a separate assembly compatibility format; inspect or export it with 'aetheris asm'.

Usage: aetheris build <file.firmament> [--output <path>] [--json]

Options:
  --output <path> Optional output STEP path; defaults to a .step file beside the source.
  --json         Emit machine-readable success/failure JSON.
  -h, --help     Show this help.

Example:
  aetheris build part.firmament
  aetheris build part.firmament --output out/part.step --json

result.stdout:
Analyze part-like STEP geometry and topology.

Usage: aetheris analyze <file.step> [--face <id>] [--edge <id>] [--vertex <id>] [--json]
   or: aetheris analyze map <file.step> (--plane <xy|xz|yz> --direction <+x|-x|+y|-y|+z|-z> | --views six --llm) --resolution <NxM> [--point <u,v>] [--rank-probes|--evidence-bundle] --json
   or: aetheris analyze section <file.step> (--xy|--xz|--yz) --offset <value> --json

Options (summary mode):
  --face <id>     Inspect one face.
  --edge <id>     Inspect one edge.
  --vertex <id>   Inspect one vertex.
  --json          Emit machine-readable JSON (default output is human-readable text).
  -h, --help      Show this help.

Rules:
  - At most one of --face, --edge, --vertex may be supplied.
  - Use 'aetheris analyze map --help' for orthographic map options.
  - Use 'aetheris analyze section --help' for section options.
  - Use 'aetheris analyze volume --help' for volume options.
  - Assembly-like multi-root STEP is rejected here with a route hint to assembly extraction/import.

Examples:
  aetheris analyze part.step
  aetheris analyze part.step --json
  aetheris analyze part.step --face 12
  aetheris analyze part.step --face 12 --json
  aetheris analyze map part.step --right --rows 20 --cols 30 --json
  aetheris analyze section part.step --yz --offset 1.25 --json

Usage: aetheris verify <file.firmament|file.step> [--expected-volume <value>] [--cad-assistant] [--cad-assistant-path <path>] [--timeout <seconds>] [--evidence-dir <path>] [--require-external] [--json]

Firmament input is built first; STEP input is reimported directly for independent B-rep mass properties and optional external display inspection.
The report is hash-tied to artifacts/verification/<fixture>/<sha256>/ by default.

Options:
  --expected-volume <value>   Compare independent measured volume with external analytic evidence; never used by the evaluator.
  --cad-assistant              Launch configured CAD Assistant for external display observation.
  --cad-assistant-path <path> Explicit CAD Assistant executable; otherwise AETHERIS_CAD_ASSISTANT_PATH and two standard install paths are checked.
  --timeout <seconds>          External inspection timeout (default 30).
  --evidence-dir <path>        Override hash-tied evidence directory.
  --require-external           Return exit 2 when CAD Assistant is unavailable.
  --json                       Emit the unified report on stdout.

result.stdout:
Experimentally reconstruct an approximate, predominantly quad SurfaceMeshDocument from a triangle surface.
This is shrink-wrap/structured remeshing, not CAD feature or design-intent recognition.

Usage: aetheris reconstruct mesh <input.ply> --mode fast --out <output.obj> [--report <report.json>] [--error-ply <samples.ply>] [--json]

Supported input: ASCII PLY containing triangle faces. Output: deterministic OBJ, optional compact JSON, and optional colored error-sample PLY.
Fast uses scale-derived tolerance, bounded local matching, cached correspondence, bounded quality sampling, and no global atlas search.

result.stdout:
Analyze STEP body as an orthographic depth/thickness map.

Usage: aetheris analyze map <file.step> (--plane <xy|xz|yz> --direction <+x|-x|+y|-y|+z|-z> | --views six --llm) --resolution <NxM> [--point <u,v>] [--rank-probes|--evidence-bundle] --json

Required:
  either --plane <xy|xz|yz> with --direction <axis>, exactly one legacy view, or --views six --llm.
  legacy views: --top | --bottom | --front | --back | --left | --right
  --rows <N>       Positive integer row count.
  --cols <N>       Positive integer column count.
  --resolution NxM Alternative to --cols N --rows M.
  --json           Required output mode.

Six-view convention:
  top xy/-z, bottom xy/+z, right yz/-x, left yz/+x, back xz/+y, front xz/-y.

Example:
  aetheris analyze map part.step --top --rows 48 --cols 64 --json
  aetheris analyze map part.step --views six --resolution 16x16 --llm --rank-probes --json
